doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

title: Jazz parties and the cruise as friendly gatherings
summary: Jazz parties and the cruise avoid competition and let musicians talk at length.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Have you ever done any of the jazz parties?
Yeah I’ve done some of those, sure. Yeah. Those are fun.
They are. And they don’t usually descend into that.
Right. Exactly. And that’s what — the jazz cruise is like that as well. Everybody’s just kind of like having a great time and nobody’s got an agenda.
Right. Leave your agenda at the —
Yeah we got to go on one of those things. I thought I was in heaven. I didn’t know such a thing existed. You know here’s Joe Williams and Oscar Peterson and Nat Adderley.

Yeah. And it’s great for the musicians too, because it’s rare that we have more than just time to say hello, how’s it going, what’s been going on. Actually when I’m on the ship, you know, you can have long, you know, fairly meaningful conversations with these guys that you haven’t really had a chance to say much other than how’s the weather. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
Yeah. And you don’t have to talk about music all the time. Because you get a little bit more time.
